title: openfilm.json
description: How OpenFilm shows a skill, a workbench or a connector, and what it declares it does. It sits beside SKILL.md in the item's folder. Every field is optional; OpenFilm leaves out anything missing or wrong. A listed skill also passes scripts/check.mjs, which asks for more (see SPEC.md).

version.description: x.y.z, raised with every change; the commit is tagged v<version>.

kind.description: For a skill: a way of turning material into a film, or a kind of look.

icon.description: A mark's name. A listed skill uses one of copy, scissors, monitor, shapes, pip, pen, film, music, presentation, layers.

preview.description: A short video in the folder, played on its page instead of the cover.

order.description: Lower comes first, among OpenFilm's own.

summary.description: One line on what it does, by language.

details.description: A few lines: who it is for and what it does, by language.

needs.description: What it needs beyond OpenFilm, by language: "FFmpeg 8".

platforms.description: The computers it runs on; without it, every one. OpenFilm does not install it elsewhere.

requires.description: The skills an agent reads before this one, by name.

tab.description: Shown as a tab of the library drawer instead of as a workbench: true, or its own name and mark.

blocks.description: The blocks its workbench is laid out in: another workbench's name to use its arrangement, or the blocks it draws and those of other workbenches it borrows ("owner:id").

category.description: What it helps make: material (shots, pictures, sets), edit (cutting and reviewing), picture (color, motion, compositing), sound, recipe (a whole way of making a kind of film) or tool.

difficulty.description: How hard it is to start with: 1 anyone at once, 5 a professional's.

ease.description: How little work a result takes once started: 1 all by hand, 5 a sentence.

audience.description: Who it is for, by language.

cost.description: Whether using it costs money: generation, when it makes media with a paid service.

permissions.description: What it does beyond reading its own folder, each with a reason people are shown before they add it. network is enforced: a page reaches only these hosts. The rest are declared and shown, and reviewed against what the code does.

network.description: Enforced. The hosts its page may reach, over https: a host name, or every host under one with a leading "*.". A page reaches nothing else. Scripts and programs are reviewed against the same list.

project.description: Declared. Whether it reads or changes the project's files. OpenFilm asks the person before a plugin changes a project.

program.description: Declared. It runs a program of its own on the computer (package.json scripts.start). OpenFilm asks the person before it starts.

secrets.description: Declared. The keys it uses, each by name.

agent.description: Declared. Whether its brief has the agent run its scripts, which run with the agent's own permissions.

words.description: Words by language (en, zh-CN, ja, ko, es), or one string, read as English.

why.description: Why it needs this, by language, in a sentence people read before they add it.
